use: A computer system at work, or how a place is set up, like how a bar charges or how ordering works.

example.romaji: Kono mise, dou iu shisutemu na no?
example.ja: この店、どういうシステムなの？
example.english: How does it work at this place?

examplePolite.romaji: Kono mise wa dou iu shisutemu desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この店はどういうシステムですか？
examplePolite.english: How does it work here?

use: Your plans for a day or week, or the timetable for a project or trip.

example.romaji: Raishuu no sukejuuru, dou natteru?
example.ja: 来週のスケジュール、どうなってる？
example.english: What's your schedule like next week?

examplePolite.romaji: Raishuu no sukejuuru wa dou natte imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 来週のスケジュールはどうなっていますか？
examplePolite.english: What does your schedule look like next week?

notes: Yotei is the everyday word for one plan: ashita yotei aru? = got plans tomorrow?

use: Staying late at work after normal hours; zangyou suru = to work overtime.

example.romaji: Kyou mo zangyou de osoku naru.
example.ja: 今日も残業で遅くなる。
example.english: I'll be home late again, working overtime.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou mo zangyou de osoku narimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日も残業で遅くなります。
examplePolite.english: I'll be late again today because of overtime.

example.romaji: Shukudai, mou zenbu owatta no?
example.ja: 宿題、もう全部終わったの？
example.english: Have you finished all your homework already?

examplePolite.romaji: Shukudai wa mou zenbu owarimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 宿題はもう全部終わりましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you finished all your homework?

notes: At work, shukudai ni sasete kudasai = let me take that away and get back to you.

example.romaji: Shimekiri, ashita made da yo.
example.ja: 締め切り、明日までだよ。
example.english: The deadline's tomorrow, you know.

examplePolite.romaji: Shimekiri wa ashita made desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 締め切りは明日までですよ。
examplePolite.english: The deadline is tomorrow.

notes: Shimekiri ni maniau = make the deadline; maniawanai = miss it.

example.romaji: Tsuukin ni ichijikan kakaru n da.
example.ja: 通勤に一時間かかるんだ。
example.english: My commute takes an hour.

examplePolite.romaji: Tsuukin ni ichijikan kakarimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 通勤に一時間かかります。
examplePolite.english: My commute takes an hour.

notes: Tsuugaku is commuting to school. Tsuukin suru = to commute; densha de tsuukin = commute by train.

use: Short for yuukyuu kyuuka; you 'take' it: yuukyuu o toru.

example.romaji: Raishuu, yuukyuu totte ryokou suru n da.
example.ja: 来週、有給取って旅行するんだ。
example.english: I'm taking paid leave next week to go on a trip.

examplePolite.romaji: Raishuu, yuukyuu o totte ryokou shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来週、有給を取って旅行します。
examplePolite.english: I'm taking paid leave next week for a trip.

english: days off in a row; long weekend
use: Two or more days off in a row, especially around public holidays.

example.romaji: Kondo no renkyuu, doko ka iku?
example.ja: 今度の連休、どこか行く？
example.english: Going anywhere over the long weekend?

examplePolite.romaji: Kondo no renkyuu wa doko ka ikimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今度の連休はどこか行きますか？
examplePolite.english: Are you going anywhere over the long weekend?

notes: Sanrenkyuu = a three-day weekend. Golden Week in early May is the big one.

use: For how you, your body, a machine or things in general are doing; choushi dou? = how's it going?

example.romaji: Hisashiburi! Saikin, choushi dou?
example.ja: 久しぶり！最近、調子どう？
example.english: Long time no see! How've you been?

examplePolite.romaji: Ohisashiburi desu. Saikin, choushi wa dou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: お久しぶりです。最近、調子はどうですか？
examplePolite.english: It's been a while. How have you been?

notes: Choushi ga warui = not feeling well, or not working right. Choushi ni noru = get carried away.

use: A cut or scar on skin, a scratch on an object, or hurt feelings.

example.romaji: Kono kizu, dou shita no?
example.ja: この傷、どうしたの？
example.english: How did you get this cut?

examplePolite.romaji: Sono kizu wa dou shita n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: その傷はどうしたんですか？
examplePolite.english: How did you get that cut?

notes: Kega is the injury itself; kizu is the cut or mark you can see. Kizutsuku = to get hurt, often feelings.

use: You 'drink' medicine in Japanese, even pills: kusuri o nomu.

example.romaji: Kusuri nonde, hayaku neta hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: 薬飲んで、早く寝た方がいいよ。
example.english: Take some medicine and get to bed early.

examplePolite.romaji: Kusuri o nonde, hayaku neta hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 薬を飲んで、早く寝た方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You should take some medicine and go to bed early.

notes: Kusuriya or yakkyoku = pharmacy. In crime talk it can mean illegal drugs.

english: how you feel (health); condition; how something works
use: Mostly asked about health: guai ga warui = feel sick.

example.romaji: Daijoubu? Guai warui no?
example.ja: 大丈夫？具合悪いの？
example.english: Are you okay? Not feeling well?

examplePolite.romaji: Daijoubu desu ka? Guai ga warui n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 大丈夫ですか？具合が悪いんですか？
examplePolite.english: Are you all right? Are you feeling unwell?

notes: Close to choushi, but guai leans toward feeling physically ill. Konna guai ni = like this, this way.

english: to get hurt; to be injured
use: Any physical injury, from a scraped knee to a bad accident.

example.romaji: Daijoubu? Doko mo kega shinakatta?
example.ja: 大丈夫？どこもケガしなかった？
example.english: You okay? You didn't hurt yourself anywhere?

examplePolite.romaji: Daijoubu desu ka? Doko mo kega shimasen deshita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 大丈夫ですか？どこもケガしませんでしたか？
examplePolite.english: Are you all right? You weren't hurt anywhere?

notes: The noun kega = an injury: kega wa nai? = anyone hurt? Kizu is the cut or wound itself.

english: to go into hospital; to be hospitalised
use: As a patient staying overnight or longer; nyuuin shite iru = is in hospital.

example.romaji: Sobo ga kinou kara nyuuin shiteru n da.
example.ja: 祖母が昨日から入院してるんだ。
example.english: My grandma's been in hospital since yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Sobo ga kinou kara nyuuin shite iru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 祖母が昨日から入院しているんです。
examplePolite.english: My grandmother has been in hospital since yesterday.

notes: Opposite: taiin suru. Just seeing a doctor is byouin ni iku.

use: Usually means a fever: netsu ga aru = have a temperature.

example.romaji: Chotto netsu aru kara, kyou wa yasumu ne.
example.ja: ちょっと熱あるから、今日は休むね。
example.english: I've got a bit of a fever, so I'm taking today off.

examplePolite.romaji: Sukoshi netsu ga aru node, kyou wa yasumimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 少し熱があるので、今日は休みます。
examplePolite.english: I have a slight fever, so I'll take today off.

notes: Netsu o hakaru = take your temperature; netsu ga sagatta = the fever's gone down.

example.romaji: Dareka, hayaku kyuukyuusha yonde!
example.ja: 誰か、早く救急車呼んで！
example.english: Someone, quick, call an ambulance!

examplePolite.romaji: Sumimasen, kyuukyuusha o yonde kudasai!
examplePolite.ja: すみません、救急車を呼んでください！
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, please call an ambulance!

notes: Kyuukyuusha o yobu = call an ambulance. In Japan the number is 119.

use: The patient 'receives' it (shujutsu o ukeru), though casually people say shujutsu suru too.

example.romaji: Raigetsu, hiza no shujutsu suru n da.
example.ja: 来月、膝の手術するんだ。
example.english: I'm having knee surgery next month.

examplePolite.romaji: Raigetsu, hiza no shujutsu o ukemasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来月、膝の手術を受けます。
examplePolite.english: I'm having knee surgery next month.

notes: Shujutsu wa seikou shita = the operation went well.

use: Tests at a hospital, or checks on goods and bags; kensa o ukeru = have tests done.

example.romaji: Ashita, byouin de kensa ga aru n da.
example.ja: 明日、病院で検査があるんだ。
example.english: I've got some tests at the hospital tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: Ashita, byouin de kensa o ukemasu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日、病院で検査を受けます。
examplePolite.english: I'm having some tests at the hospital tomorrow.

notes: Kensa no kekka = test results. A school test is tesuto, not kensa.

use: Ongoing care for an illness or injury, including dental work.

example.romaji: Ima, ha no chiryou ni kayotteru.
example.ja: 今、歯の治療に通ってる。
example.english: I'm going in regularly for dental work right now.

examplePolite.romaji: Ima, ha no chiryou ni kayotte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今、歯の治療に通っています。
examplePolite.english: I'm getting dental treatment at the moment.

notes: Chiryou o ukeru = get treatment. Naoru (to heal) is the result you hope for.

english: to leave hospital; to be discharged

example.romaji: Haha, raishuu taiin dekiru tte.
example.ja: 母、来週退院できるって。
example.english: They say Mum can leave hospital next week.

examplePolite.romaji: Haha wa raishuu taiin dekiru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 母は来週退院できるそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear my mother can leave hospital next week.

notes: Opposite of nyuuin suru. Taiin omedetou = congrats on getting out of hospital.
